{
  "architecture_summary": "EConverter is a self-hosted, enterprise-grade document conversion and intelligence platform built on ASP.NET Core, with a Blazor Server (Radzen) presentation layer and an optional standalone worker microservice. The codebase implements Clean Architecture / Domain-Driven Design in seven projects: Domain (aggregates and invariants), Contracts (transport DTOs and queue messages), Application (use-case contracts), Processing.Abstractions and Security (shared building blocks), Infrastructure (all adapters), Web (composition root plus in-process background workers), and Workers/DocumentWorker. Persistence is unified in a single EF Core AppDbContext over Npgsql, merging ASP.NET Core Identity tables with the domain schema and evolving through a linear migration chain. Asynchronous processing runs on a lease-based ProcessingJob state machine, dispatched via RabbitMQ with graceful degradation to NoOpQueuePublisher and a polling loop, so the broker is an accelerator rather than a hard dependency. A substantial local, zero-egress intelligence stack (BM25 inverted index, HNSW vector index, RAG retrieval orchestration, auto-classification, copilot chat, dossier export) executes in-process, while ExternalAiClient optionally reaches OpenAI, Gemini, Claude or local endpoints with streaming SSE/NDJSON normalization. Security is first-class: authorization keyed on stable internal entity IDs rather than identity-provider subjects, dual authentication (Local + EntraId), domain-enforced document ownership, AES-GCM storage encryption, malware/zip-bomb/file-signature guarding, and language-code sanitization against tessdata path injection. The main structural tension is that several high-value orchestrators live in Infrastructure rather than the Application layer, and one minimal-API endpoint file mixes transport with inline document conversion logic.",

### Workflow Research Report
Contains static analysis results of the codebase and business process analysis.

```json
"# System Workflow Analysis\n\n## 1. Main Workflow\n\n- **Workflow Name**: Asynchronous Conversion Job Processing Flow\n- **Description**: The central value-producing workflow of EConverter. A user (via the Blazor UI, the minimal API, or the standalone `DocumentWorker`) requests a format conversion — DOCX→PDF, PDF→DOCX, image OCR, or compression. The system materializes that request as a `ProcessingJob` aggregate with a lease-based state machine, dispatches a `JobMessage` through RabbitMQ (or degrades gracefully to polling), and a worker executes the full conversion transaction: streaming the input from encrypted storage, verifying its SHA-256 hash, invoking the selected `IDocumentProcessor`, encrypting and uploading the output, committing state transitions, pushing SignalR progress notifications, and finally aggregating batch-level completion.\n\n  This workflow is what allows the platform to absorb large document backlogs asynchronously without blocking interactive users, and its lease/retry semantics make it resilient to worker crashes and broker unavailability.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"User selects converter + source docs<br/>(BatchConversionDialog.razor)\"] --> B[\"IProcessingService<br/>create job / batch\"]\n    B --> C[\"ProcessingService<br/>validate access via security abstractions\"]\n    C --> D[\"ProcessingJob aggregate<br/>(Pending)\"]\n    D --> E[\"Persist via AppDbContext<br/>(EF Core / Npgsql)\"]\n    E --> F{\"Messaging enabled?\"}\n    F -->|Yes| G[\"RabbitMqJobDispatcher<br/>publish JobMessage\"]\n    F -->|No| H[\"NoOpQueuePublisher<br/>→ polling fallback\"]\n    G --> I[\"JobProcessorWorker / DocumentWorker<br/>lease job (Claim)\"]\n    H --> I\n    I --> J[\"Open encrypted input stream<br/>(AES-GCM storage)\"]\n    J --> K[\"Compute SHA-256<br/>verify hash\"]\n    K --> L[\"Select IDocumentProcessor<br/>via converter catalog\"]\n    L --> M[\"Execute conversion<br/>(Office / PDF / OCR / Image / Compress)\"]\n    M --> N{\"Conversion<br/>succeeded?\"}\n    N -->|No| O[\"MarkFailed<br/>(error code + retry eligibility)\"]\n    N -->|Yes| P[\"Encrypt + upload output<br/>(AES-GCM)\"]\n    P --> Q[\"Register output document<br/>as new version\"]\n    Q --> R[\"MarkCompleted\"]\n    R --> S[\"JobNotificationService<br/>broadcast over SignalR\"]\n    O --> S\n    S --> T[\"CheckBatchCompletionAsync<br/>aggregate batch terminal state\"]\n    T --> U[\"Client sees final status<br/>(Completed / Failed / Cancelled)\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. **Request Collection** — `BatchConversionDialog.razor` gathers converter selection, source documents, and output options; submits as strongly typed request records.\n  2. **Use-Case Contract** — `IProcessingService` exposes job/batch creation, status query, and cancellation as the single application-facing gateway.\n  3. **Access Validation + Persistence** — `ProcessingService` validates access against security abstractions, writes `ProcessingJob` entities through `AppDbContext`, and dispatches `JobMessage` payloads via `IQueuePublisher` (with `NoOpQueuePublisher` fallback).\n  4. **State Machine Enforcement** — `ProcessingJobLifecycle` (in `ProcessingJobStatus.cs`) is the single authority on legal transitions, terminal states, and retryable error codes; no illegal transition can occur anywhere in the system.\n  5. **Queue Dispatch or Poll** — `RabbitMqJobDispatcher` publishes to the broker; when the consumer is disabled, the worker polls the database instead.\n  6. **Worker Lease + Stream** — `JobProcessorWorker` (web host) or `Worker.cs` (standalone service) calls `Claim`, opens the encrypted input stream, and computes the SHA-256 hash.\n  7. **Conversion Execution** — The `IDocumentProcessor` implementation runs the concrete transformation; `RenewLease` / `UpdateProgress` keep the lease alive and push progress.\n  8. **Encrypted Output Upload** — Output is encrypted via `AesGcmStorageEncryptionService`, uploaded through `IDocumentStorage`, and recorded on the output entity.\n  9. **SignalR Notification** — `JobNotificationService` broadcasts progress/completion to subscribed Blazor circuits via `ProcessingHub`.\n  10. **Batch Aggregation** — `CheckBatchCompletionAsync` rolls per-job outcomes into a batch-level terminal state.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Other Important Workflows\n\n### 2.1 Document Upload and Lifecycle Management Flow\n\n- **Description**: The foundational workflow everything else depends on. A user uploads a document through the Blazor explorer or the `/api/documents` minimal API. The system authenticates the caller, resolves the stable internal user ID (deliberately decoupled from any identity-provider subject — a documented security decision), enforces ownership at the domain level, sanitizes the filename, scans for malware/zip-bomb/EICAR signatures, stores the bytes under AES-GCM encryption, and registers a versioned `Document` aggregate. Rename, move, folder CRUD, soft delete, restore, and purge all follow the same ownership-and-audit spine.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"Upload request<br/>(/api/documents or Documents.razor)\"] --> B[\"HttpContextUserContext<br/>authenticate + resolve stable entity ID\"]\n    B --> C[\"Input hardening<br/>FileSignatureDetector / ZipBombGuard / EicarSignatureDetector / FileNameSanitizer\"]\n    C --> D{\"Malware scan<br/>(ClamAvScanner)\"}\n    D -->|Infected| E[\"Reject upload<br/>+ audit event\"]\n    D -->|Clean| F[\"DocumentService<br/>validate ownership (IsOwnedBy)\"]\n    F --> G[\"Compute SHA-256<br/>+ storage key\"]\n    G --> H[\"FileSystemDocumentStorage<br/>encrypt (AES-GCM) + write bytes\"]\n    H --> I[\"AppDbContext<br/>persist Document + DocumentVersion\"]\n    I --> J[\"AuditService<br/>record mutation\"]\n    J --> K[\"Document appears in user explorer\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. Authentication and stable-ID resolution via `HttpContextUserContext` / `AppClaimsTransformation`.\n  2. Pre-pipeline hardening: file-signature detection, zip-bomb guard, EICAR detection, filename sanitization.\n  3. ClamAV malware scan via `IMalwareScanner`.\n  4. Ownership enforcement and lifecycle rules in `DocumentService` (cyclomatic complexity 135 — the densest branching hub in the system).\n  5. AES-GCM encryption + storage write through `IDocumentStorage`.\n  6. EF Core persistence of the aggregate and its version row.\n  7. Audit event emission for compliance review.\n\n- **Note on structural tension**: `DocumentEndpoints.cs` (902 lines) mixes transport concerns with inline OpenXml/PdfSharp DOCX→PDF conversion logic — a direct-DOCX-to-PDF path that bypasses the job pipeline. This is the primary place where the architecture's layering intent is violated.\n\n### 2.2 Document Intelligence Indexing and RAG Question Answering Flow\n\n- **Description**: The differentiating capability. After a document enters the system, the indexing pipeline extracts text (with OCR fallback for scanned pages), chunks it with multilingual handling, generates embeddings, and upserts both a BM25 lexical index and an HNSW vector index. A user then asks a natural-language question in the Copilot UI; the `RagRetrievalOrchestrator` transforms the query, performs hybrid retrieval, fuses results (RRF), diversifies with MMR, optionally reranks, expands context, and synthesizes a grounded answer with citations — optionally exported as a PDF/DOCX/XLSX/Markdown dossier.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"Document processed / stored\"] --> B[\"DocumentIndexingWorker<br/>dequeue via bounded channel\"]\n    B --> C[\"Text extraction<br/>(OCR fallback: TesseractOcrEngine)\"]\n    C --> D[\"DocumentIntelligenceService<br/>validate access + chunk content\"]\n    D --> E[\"MultilingualChunkProcessor<br/>+ DocumentLanguageDetector\"]\n    E --> F[\"Generate embeddings\"]\n    F --> G[\"Batch upsert<br/>vector chunks + intelligence index\"]\n    G --> H1[\"Bm25InvertedIndex<br/>(lexical)\"]\n    G --> H2[\"HnswVectorIndex<br/>(semantic)\"]\n    I[\"User asks question<br/>(Copilot.razor)\"] --> J[\"RagRetrievalOrchestrator<br/>query transformation\"]\n    J --> K[\"Hybrid retrieval<br/>BM25 + HNSW\"]\n    H1 --> K\n    H2 --> K\n    K --> L[\"Fuse (RRF) + diversify (MMR)<br/>+ optional LLM rerank + context expansion\"]\n    L --> M{\"Local synthesis<br/>or external provider?\"}\n    M -->|Local| N[\"Zero-egress answer synthesis\"]\n    M -->|External| O[\"ExternalAiClient<br/>SSE/NDJSON streaming parse\"]\n    N --> P[\"Grounded answer + citations\"]\n    O --> P\n    P --> Q[\"CopilotDossierExporter<br/>PDF / DOCX / XLSX / Markdown\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. Bounded-channel indexing dequeue via `DocumentIndexingWorker`.\n  2. OCR-assisted text extraction when pages are scanned.\n  3. Chunking, language detection, and embedding generation.\n  4. Dual index upsert: BM25 inverted index (thread-safe, tombstone-based deletion) and HNSW ANN graph.\n  5. Copilot question intake with session/memory persistence.\n  6. Query transformation → hybrid retrieval → RRF fusion → MMR diversification → rerank → context expansion.\n  7. Grounded synthesis with traceable sources, locally by default, externally when policy permits.\n  8. Optional dossier export to four publication-ready formats.\n\n- **Quality assurance**: `RagBenchmarkRunner` provides a reproducible 120-question evaluation harness measuring Recall@K, MRR, nDCG, context precision/recall, and faithfulness — with deterministic GUID chunk identity for regression comparison.\n\n### 2.3 PDF Editing and Annotation Flow\n\n- **Description**: An interactive authoring workflow that converts the platform from a converter into a document workspace. The user opens a PDF in `PdfEditor.razor` (rendered in-browser via bundled pdf.js), applies page-structure and annotation operations — reorder, rotate, add/remove pages, highlight, ink, sticky note, stamp, watermark, redaction, form fields, digital signature — and saves. `PdfEngine` translates the operation DTOs deterministically into PdfSharp drawing calls, and the result is persisted as a new document version.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"PdfEditor.razor<br/>render via pdf.js\"] --> B[\"User applies edit operations<br/>(toolbars / dialogs)\"]\n    B --> C[\"PdfEditOperationDto[]\"]\n    C --> D[\"EditorEndpoints<br/>accept DTOs\"]\n    D --> E[\"PdfEngine<br/>classify operations\"]\n    E --> F1[\"ApplyPageStructureOperations<br/>add / remove / rotate / reorder\"]\n    E --> F2[\"ApplyAnnotationOperations<br/>highlight / ink / note / underline\"]\n    E --> F3[\"Draw operations<br/>text / shape / image / stamp / watermark / redaction\"]\n    F1 --> G[\"Mutated PDF document\"]\n    F2 --> G\n    F3 --> G\n    G --> H[\"DocumentService<br/>persist as new version + hash + storage key\"]\n    H --> I[\"Encrypted storage write\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. In-browser rendering through bundled pdf.js.\n  2. Operation collection from editor dialogs (merge, extract, OCR, stamp, watermark, password, signature).\n  3. DTO transport to `EditorEndpoints`.\n  4. Operation classification and dispatch in `PdfEngine`.\n  5. PdfSharp rendering with `SystemFontResolver` for consistent fonts.\n  6. Versioned persistence through `DocumentService`.\n\n### 2.4 Administration, Identity and Audit Flow\n\n- **Description**: Governs the running platform. Users authenticate via local credentials or EntraId federation; provider claims are transformed onto a stable internal identity. Administrators manage users, roles, departments, the converter catalog with limits, and system settings, and review the security audit log. Authorization is keyed on the internal entity ID rather than any provider subject — ensuring permissions survive identity-provider churn.\n\n- **Flow Diagram**:\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"Login<br/>(local or EntraId OIDC)\"] --> B[\"AppClaimsTransformation<br/>map provider claims → stable internal identity\"]\n    B --> C{\"Administrator?\"}\n    C -->|No| D[\"Standard user surface\"]\n    C -->|Yes| E[\"AdminService\"]\n    E --> F1[\"UsersAndDepartments.razor<br/>create users, assign roles/departments\"]\n    E --> F2[\"ConvertersCatalog.razor<br/>converter availability + limits\"]\n    E --> F3[\"SystemSettings.razor<br/>read/write settings\"]\n    F1 --> G[\"User aggregate invariants<br/>+ AuditService\"]\n    F2 --> H[\"Constrain what ProcessingService may schedule\"]\n    F3 --> I[\"SystemSetting persistence\"]\n    G --> J[\"SecurityAuditLog.razor<br/>query + display audit events\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps**:\n  1. Dual authentication (Local + EntraId) with claims transformation to stable internal identity.\n  2. `User` aggregate enforcing identity, role membership, and profile state invariants.\n  3. Administrative mutations through `AdminService`.\n  4. Converter catalog and limits constraining downstream job scheduling.\n  5. Audit event persistence and review via `SecurityAuditLog.razor`.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Workflow Insights\n\n### Operational Patterns\n\n- **Queue as accelerator, not dependency.** RabbitMQ is optional by design: `NoOpQueuePublisher` and database polling ensure the conversion pipeline degrades gracefully. This is a deliberate resilience decision, not an oversight — operators can run the platform without a broker.\n- **Single authority for state.** `ProcessingJobLifecycle` centralizes every transition, terminal-state, and retry-eligibility decision. No component can bypass it. This is the strongest architectural invariant in the processing domain.\n- **Authorization anchored on stable internal IDs.** Both the `User` aggregate and `ProcessingService` deliberately key on the internal entity ID rather than the identity-provider subject — a security decision explicitly documented in source. Permissions survive EntraId re-provisioning.\n- **Security hardening at the boundary.** Filename sanitization, file-signature detection, EICAR matching, zip-bomb guarding, ClamAV scanning, and tessdata language-code sanitization all fire before documents enter the pipeline. Trust boundaries are enforced at ingress, not scattered downstream.\n- **Zero-egress by default, external by exception.** `IDocumentIntelligenceService` explicitly constrains core intelligence to in-process execution; `ExternalAiClient` is an opt-in gateway. This inverts the usual SaaS AI posture and is the platform's primary compliance differentiator.\n- **Lease-based work distribution.** `Claim` / `RenewLease` / retry-eligibility semantics make the worker fleet crash-tolerant and horizontally scalable without a distributed lock manager.\n\n### Optimization Opportunities\n\n1. **Extract inline conversion from `DocumentEndpoints.cs`.** The 902-line endpoint file contains a self-contained OpenXml/PdfSharp DOCX→PDF path that bypasses the job pipeline, duplicating logic that already lives in `OfficeDocumentProcessor`. Moving it into the processor (and routing through `ProcessingService`) would eliminate a maintenance fork and restore layering integrity.\n2. **Relocate high-value orchestrators from Infrastructure to Application.** `DocumentIntelligenceService` (~6,000 lines), `RagRetrievalOrchestrator` (4,040 lines), and `PdfEngine` currently live in Infrastructure despite being use-case logic. This inverts Clean Architecture's dependency direction and makes them harder to unit-test without the full adapter stack.\n3. **Decompose `DocumentService`.** With 27 members and cyclomatic complexity 135, it concentrates every document branching rule in one place. Splitting by operation family (lifecycle mutations vs. versioning vs. storage coordination) would reduce change-amplification risk.\n4. **Batch-completion aggregation under contention.** `CheckBatchCompletionAsync` runs at every job termination and reads/writes shared batch state. Under high parallelism, this is a plausible hotspot — a lighter terminal-check with a periodic sweep would reduce per-job overhead.\n5. **Indexing channel backpressure.** The bounded `DocumentIndexingChannel` provides backpressure, but a very large batch of indexed documents can saturate it. Exposing queue depth as a metric would let operators detect saturation before it manifests as retrieval staleness.\n6. **`Infrastructure.csproj` is a single point of build failure.** Fourteen NuGet packages (PDF, OpenXML, OCR, RabbitMQ, SkiaSharp, PKCS) pin the entire layer. Splitting adapters into separately-versioned satellite projects would reduce blast radius on library bumps and clarify licensing.\n\n### Workflow Dependencies\n\n- **Document Lifecycle → Storage → Persistence** is the foundational spine. Every other workflow (conversion, intelligence, editing, admin) ultimately reads or writes through it. Any disruption here cascades across the entire platform.\n- **Conversion → OCR → Intelligence** is the text-extraction chain. Retrieval quality depends directly on OCR fidelity; degraded OCR silently degrades RAG relevance, which makes the benchmark harness (`RagBenchmarkRunner`) the early-warning system for that dependency.\n- **Processing → Conversion Abstractions → Concrete Processors** keeps transport-agnostic conversion logic shared between the web host's `JobProcessorWorker` and the standalone `DocumentWorker`. This indirection is what enables horizontal worker scaling without coupling to the web host.\n- **Security/Identity → Document Lifecycle and Processing** is a configuration dependency, not merely a call: ownership checks in the aggregate and access validation in `ProcessingService` are the only gates enforcing authorization. Any bypass here compromises every downstream workflow.\n- **Platform Administration → Processing** is a soft dependency: converter catalog limits and settings constrain what the processing domain may schedule. Admin changes propagate algorithmically to job acceptance.\n- **Platform Composition and Hosting → everything** is the composition root. `Program.cs` wires the entire runtime; a registration error breaks all workflows simultaneously rather than one.\n\n### Discrepancies and Missing Steps (validated against documentation)\n\n- **No documented cleanup/reaper workflow** for orphaned `Processing`-state jobs whose workers died without renewing the lease. The lease mechanism implies a recovery path must exist; if it is implemented (as a hosted service), it is not represented in the provided research materials. This is a documentation gap worth confirming in source.\n- **The batch-completion aggregation** (`CheckBatchCompletionAsync`) is described at the job level; the exact semantics of batch cancellation (whether in-flight jobs are signalled, unleased pending jobs are marked `Cancelled` directly, or both) are not specified in the available research and should be verified against `BatchJob` behavior.\n- **The standalone `DocumentWorker`** executes the same conversion transaction independently of the web host, but the materials do not clarify whether it and `JobProcessorWorker` can run concurrently against the same database. Lease semantics suggest yes; this should be confirmed to avoid double-processing assumptions in deployment documentation.\n- **The Direct DOCX→PDF path in `DocumentEndpoints.cs`** is a second, undocumented entry point into conversion that does not appear in the business-flow documentation. It is a functional discrepancy between the documented asynchronous pipeline and the actual code surface, and it should either be documented or consolidated into the pipeline."
```

      "summary": "DocumentConverter.Infrastructure is the infrastructure/adapters layer of a .NET clean-architecture document conversion system, containing 12 subdirectories of concrete implementations for persistence (EF Core with SQL Server/PostgreSQL), identity, document parsing (PdfPig, OpenXml, PDFsharp, MarkItDown), OCR (Tesseract), messaging (RabbitMQ), cryptography, and rendering (SkiaSharp). It is the contracts-and-packages hub for the whole layer."

      "path": ".\\src\\DocumentConverter.Infrastructure\\AI",
      "purpose": "other",
      "subdirectory_count": 1,
      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: This directory is the AI infrastructure layer of a .NET document-converter backend. It contains a thread-safe Okapi BM25 inverted index for lexical retrieval, a channel-based bounded ingestion pipeline for background vector/index computation, and an exporter that renders executive dossiers to PDF/DOCX/XLSX/Markdown. Together they provide core retrieval, indexing and reporting capabilities used by higher-level AI query and synthesis services. This batch of the AI application layer contains the DocumentIntelligenceService implementation — a very large (≈6,000 line) sealed service that orchestrates document analysis, AI pipeline execution, global index upserts, and per-user access control. It is core backend business logic (C#/.NET) sitting between the Application AI abstractions and the Documents/Storage layers, and is clearly a hub due to its breadth of internal imports and its role as the concrete AI entry point for document analysis. The AI directory is the intelligence core of the DocumentConverter backend, housing the external LLM client (OpenAI/Gemini/Claude streaming), an offline language detector, a multilingual chunk processor for cross-lingual RAG, and a 120-question reproducible RAG benchmark runner. These C# components together deliver prompt dispatch, streaming response parsing, translation projection and retrieval-quality evaluation used by the document conversion pipeline. It also contains an HNSW subdirectory (handled in another batch) supporting vector search. The AI directory is the intelligence core of the DocumentConverter's RAG subsystem, providing the retrieval orchestration pipeline that fuses LLM query transformation, HNSW vector search, reranking, and MMR diversification into a single coherent component chain (A–H). Its files are large, dense C# backend modules that coordinate semantic chunk retrieval, translation appending, and result validation, making it the highest-value directory in this batch."

      "summary": "This directory is the EF Core persistence configuration layer of the DocumentConverter backend, containing five sealed classes that each implement IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> for every domain aggregate: identity, documents, processing pipeline, Copilot/AI, and system auditing.       "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: This directory holds the Entity Framework Core migration history for the DocumentConverter AppDbContext, defining the full relational schema of the persistence layer from the initial baseline through chat/memory, vector chunk, and document intelligence additions. Each migration is a generated pair: a timestamped migration class with Up/Down schema operations and a matching Designer snapshot of the model state at that point. Together they act as the authoritative, ordered DDL source for the identity schema plus the document conversion and copilot persistence tables. This directory contains the Entity Framework Core migration history for the DocumentConverter persistence layer, including two schema-changing migrations (adding tri-language chunk support with a Language column and widening the vector chunk Embedding column) plus their auto-generated Designer files and the current AppDbContextModelSnapshot. The migrations themselves are thin declarative schema diffs, while the Designer/snapshot files hold ~1480-line generated model definitions that describe the full database schema and serve as the source of truth for future migrations. Together they define and evolve the PostgreSQL-backed data layer for document vector chunks and embeddings."

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: Vendored third-party PDF.js library assets embedded in the ASP.NET Core web application's static file root (wwwroot/lib). This batch contains the minified PDF.js bundle, a Mozilla-authored client-side PDF rendering engine that lets browsers parse and display PDF documents without a plugin. It is infrastructure-only code: no business logic, but it is a load-bearing dependency for any PDF preview feature in DocumentConverter.Web. The pdfjs directory contains the bundled, minified PDF.js worker runtime (pdf.worker.min.js plus its license/companion file), which is a third-party frontend library used for in-browser PDF rendering. It holds no project-specific business logic, APIs, or data layer — it is a vendored dependency asset served statically to the client. The pdfjs directory contains the client-side PDF.js interactive editing engine for the Document Converter Platform. It is a single self-contained browser IIFE that exposes a global window.pdfEditor object handling PDF rendering, page manipulation, annotation operations with undo/redo, drag/resize tooling, and .NET interop via DotNetRef. It is pure frontend presentation-layer logic with no backend business or data-layer responsibilities."

      "summary": "DocumentWorker is the background processing microservice of the DocumentConverter solution — a .NET 10 worker host that consumes RabbitMQ jobs (or falls back to polling) and executes the actual document conversion pipeline: retrieve encrypted storage stream, hash, convert, encrypt/upload output, persist job state, and notify clients. It is the execution engine of the system: without it, no document is ever converted, making Worker.cs + Program.cs the operational core of the business. The Dockerfile and appsettings files define its deployment and runtime wiring (connection strings, storage root, RabbitMQ toggle)."
